name: create-loop
cost: Free (Apache 2.0). Agents use your own Claude and ChatGPT logins
works_with: Cloudroom, with the Claude Code, Codex, Pi and other agents it runs
short: Sets up a recurring Cloudroom loop: an agent checks one thing, archives itself if all is fine and reports only when you're needed.
what: You describe the job in one sentence. The skill fills in the rest from defaults: every 4 hours in your timezone, the same agent and model as the current thread, read-only access and a fresh thread for every run. It reads the files the job touches, writes a short prompt, creates the loop with `room-cli loop create` and runs it once as a test. Then it tells you the loop's name, schedule and test thread.
who: Cloudroom users who want small watchdog jobs, like checking a branch or a service every few hours. It depends on Cloudroom's `room-cli`, so it won't work in other agents.
needs: Cloudroom: the desktop app for Apple Silicon Macs (macOS 13+), Linux x64 (alpha) or Windows 11 (beta), or the core hosted on your own Ubuntu 24.04 machine
A Claude or ChatGPT login for the agents

steps.title: Get Cloudroom
steps.text: Download the app from https://www.cloudroom.dev/download. It updates itself. This skill is one of the skills every Cloudroom agent ships with.

steps.title: Or host the core yourself
steps.text: On Ubuntu 24.04. Then connect the app with your server's URL and token.
steps.code:
curl -fsSL https://cloudroom.dev/install.sh -o install.sh
sudo bash install.sh

steps.title: Ask for a loop
steps.text: In a thread, say "create loop" and describe the job. Anything you say overrides a default. It asks only when the job itself is unclear.

steps.title: Check the test run
steps.text: The skill runs the loop once and gives you its thread. After that, each run is its own thread, and it archives itself when all is fine.

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Every 4 hours, have an agent check X", with X being the one thing you want watched.

watch: Cloudroom agents run without approval prompts, so the README says to give each trusted user their own machine.
Loops are read-only by default. No edits, commits or pushes until you approve a fix.
Read `install.sh` before you run it with sudo.
Cloud agents can reach your Mac. You choose Off, Read-only, Ask first or Full.
A loop that calls paid APIs costs money each run. The skill suggests fetching only what's new since the last run.
